summary: Mon Jam (Mon Cham) is a highland ridge and viewpoint area in Mae Raem, Mae Rim, about 40 minutes from central Chiang Mai in the Tourism Authority of Thailand’s visitor information. Dawn can bring cool air and valley mist, but sunrise visibility depends on weather, and access is spread across viewpoints, gardens and businesses rather than one clearly documented attraction.
whyGo: See the mountain landscape and Nong Hoi Royal Project farming area in the cool season.
Early light and possible valley mist give the outing a different feel from a midday visit.
Pair the viewpoint with Mae Rim stops if you have a driver and a full morning.
bestFor: Travellers who enjoy mountain scenery and are comfortable with an early start.
Visitors with a car, motorbike or pre-arranged private driver.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed sunrise, clear view or scheduled public transport.
Steep walking or winding mountain roads would make the outing uncomfortable.
duration: Planning estimate: allow 3–4 hours including the drive from Chiang Mai, viewpoint time and return; allow longer if stopping at gardens or cafés. The official tourism source describes the drive as about 40 minutes, but dawn road conditions and exact destination affect timing.
cost: No single Mon Jam admission fee or current official tariff was found. Some gardens, photo areas, food and parking may charge separately; confirm prices with the specific venue and driver before setting out. Transport is extra.
hours: No authoritative site-wide opening hours were verified. Dawn access may depend on the particular viewpoint, farm or business, so confirm it directly before planning a pre-sunrise arrival.
bestTime: The Tourism Authority of Thailand identifies October–February as the best season. December is a popular cool-season month; going early may reduce some daytime traffic, but weekend and holiday crowds remain possible.
gettingThere: The Tourism Authority recommends travelling by car and describes the road as lateritic. Arrange a private car/driver or drive yourself; public transport to the ridge and a reliable dawn return were not verified. Roads are steep and winding, so allow a buffer and avoid riding beyond your comfort or license.
booking: There is no verified central ticket or reservation system for the viewpoint area. Contact the specific garden, accommodation or Royal Project Nong Hoi before going, especially to confirm early access. Pre-arrange a return ride and agree on waiting time and charges.
accessibility: Access varies by venue. The area includes sloping roads and viewpoints; a current step-free route, accessible toilets and parking close to viewing points were not verified. Ask the particular stop about surfaces, gradients and drop-off access.
practicalTips: Confirm that your chosen viewpoint is open before sunrise; do not assume all businesses open at the same time.
Bring a warm layer, grippy shoes, water and a small amount of cash.
Mist can obscure the view, so keep a flexible plan and avoid treating sunrise as guaranteed.
Ask the driver to wait or agree on an exact pickup point and return time before leaving the city.
decemberNotes: December falls within the official October–February recommended season, but it is also a busy period. Expect cooler conditions at elevation than in Chiang Mai city, while treating temperature and mist as weather-dependent. No specific December 2026 event or special opening schedule was verified.
uncertainties: No official source located that defines one public sunrise viewpoint, its exact opening time or a single admission price.
Current garden/photo area fees, parking charges and dawn transport prices vary and should be checked with the selected provider.
Visibility, traffic, road conditions and crowd levels on the travel date cannot be guaranteed.
